title: Drive-by with a hard brake
one_liner: Travel past a building, then a three-phase brake that slams the frame onto it.
when: A shot has to travel past something and stop hard ON it - an arrival, a reveal, a there-it-is beat. Not for gentle settles.
how: Pick a FRONTO-PARALLEL plate, shot square on, with both buildings already square on in it. Sliding a window across any other photograph gives a pan, not travel. Choosing the plate is most of this rig.

camrig.py report drive_by_brake --preset

, and read it BEFORE rendering: phase 2 must sustain a velocity above cruise, phase 3 must exceed phase 2.

knobs.grip: how hard the brake bites (3.9 here)
knobs.freq: spring frequency of the operator body (0.82)
knobs.roll_deg: wrist roll at full lean, in degrees (1.25)

gotcha: The brake is a BODY, not a curve. The car slows but the operator does not, so the framing ACCELERATES through the brake and the snap back is the fastest move in the shot. Three hand-drawn curves drift out of agreement with each other; one damped spring cannot.
